questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 5 cm and height 13 cm. What is its total surface area? (use π ≈ 3.14, round to 1 decimal place)
questions.why: Total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2×3.14×25 + 2×3.14×5×13 = 157.0 + 408.2 = 565.2 cm². The distractor 565.5 cm² comes from a small rounding slip in one of the two parts, and 408.2 cm² is just the curved surface area alone (forgetting the two circular ends). Always add both parts together.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Weimar Republic's constitution gave equal voting rights to all adult men AND women from 1919 — very progressive for its time. Why does this fact matter when explaining Weimar's instability?
options: It shows the republic was democratic in principle, but this alone didn't fix the deeper structural problems like proportional representation and Article 48
It proves the constitution had no flaws at all
It means only wealthy citizens could actually vote in practice
It shows Germany copied the British monarchy's voting system
questions.answer: It shows the republic was democratic in principle, but this alone didn't fix the deeper structural problems like proportional representation and Article 48
questions.why: Weimar was genuinely democratic on paper (universal suffrage), but democratic ideals didn't prevent instability caused by its voting system and emergency powers — the misconception is assuming 'democratic' automatically means 'stable'.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A history essay claims: 'The Great Depression caused Hitler to become Chancellor.' Why is this an oversimplification, even though the Depression was a major factor?
options: Because it skips the actual mechanism — mass unemployment drove desperate voters to extremist parties, and the Nazis exploited this crisis with promises and propaganda
Because the Depression had nothing to do with Hitler's rise
Because Hitler became Chancellor before the Depression started
Because only working-class Germans were affected by the Depression
questions.answer: Because it skips the actual mechanism — mass unemployment drove desperate voters to extremist parties, and the Nazis exploited this crisis with promises and propaganda
questions.why: Saying the Depression 'caused' Hitler's rise skips the causal chain: unemployment → loss of faith in mainstream parties → Nazi promises of work and strong leadership → increased votes. Naming just the two events without the link is weak reasoning.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Some argue Australia's post-WWII migration boom was mainly about humanitarian generosity — welcoming refugees out of kindness. Why is this an incomplete explanation?
options: Because it ignores that the government's motives were largely economic and strategic — needing workers and boosting population for security, not just kindness
Because Australia refused all refugees after WWII
Because humanitarian reasons never played any role at all
Because migration only began after 1970
questions.answer: Because it ignores that the government's motives were largely economic and strategic — needing workers and boosting population for security, not just kindness
questions.why: 'Populate or perish' combined genuine humanitarian elements with hard economic need (labour for factories) and security fears (a bigger population to defend the country). Reducing it to just kindness misses the real push factors behind policy.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.prompt: A student writing a business plan for a new phone case shop notes: 'Our main strength is our unique designs, and a threat is a big competitor opening nearby.' Which section of the plan does this information belong in?
options: SWOT analysis
Market analysis
Executive summary
Financial plan
questions.why: Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats about the business itself and its direct competitive position belong in the SWOT. Market analysis instead looks at broader industry data like customer demographics, demand trends, and pricing across the whole market.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: White blood cells called phagocytes surround and break down invading bacteria. What is this specific process called?
options: Phagocytosis
Antibody production
Vaccination
Immunity memory
questions.why: Phagocytosis is the specific name for a phagocyte engulfing and digesting a pathogen. It's different from antibody production, which is done by lymphocytes, not phagocytes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A country's population living in cities rises sharply as people move from farms to work in city factories. At the same time, a family moves permanently from another country to start a new life in that same city. Which statement correctly describes these two processes?
options: Both are examples of migration — the first is internal migration (within the country), the second is international migration (across a border)
Only the family from another country counts as migration, because migration only means crossing national borders
Only the farm-to-city movement counts as migration, because urbanisation and migration are the same thing
Neither is migration, because migration only refers to permanent moves, not moves for work
questions.answer: Both are examples of migration — the first is internal migration (within the country), the second is international migration (across a border)
questions.why: Migration simply means people moving from one place to live/work in another — it can be internal (within a country, like rural-urban migration) or international (across borders). Urbanisation is the specific pattern of a rising urban population, which here happens because of internal migration. Saying migration only means crossing borders ignores internal migration, which is on the syllabus.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 15 cm and a height of 7 cm. Slow down and work through it calmly, step by step: what is its area?
options: 52.5 cm²
105 cm²
22 cm²
44 cm²
questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 15 × 7 = 52.5 cm². Rushing and forgetting to halve gives 105 cm² — the classic mistake. Saying '½ × base × height' before multiplying stops this.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 12 cm. What is its total surface area? (use π ≈ 3.14, round to 1 decimal place)
options: 56.5 cm²
questions.why: Total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2(3.14)(9) + 2(3.14)(3)(12) = 56.5 + 226.1 = 282.6 cm². Forgetting the two circular ends leaves only 226.1 cm², a common oversight.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: During the Weimar Republic, the government sometimes printed huge amounts of money to pay its debts, which contributed to the 1923 hyperinflation crisis. What lesson does this teach about the republic's early economic management?
options: That printing money to solve short-term debt problems can destroy the value of currency and public trust
That printing more money always makes an economy stronger
That hyperinflation was caused by too few banknotes being available
That the Weimar government never printed any extra currency
questions.answer: That printing money to solve short-term debt problems can destroy the value of currency and public trust
questions.why: Excessive money printing without matching economic output caused hyperinflation — prices skyrocketed and savings became worthless, badly damaging public confidence in the young republic.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why the Great Depression specifically strengthened support for the Nazi Party, rather than just making Germans generally unhappy with all politicians?
options: The Nazis specifically promised strong leadership, jobs, and national revival, directly targeting the fears mass unemployment created
The Depression made every political party equally popular
The Depression only affected people living in rural areas, who didn't vote for the Nazis
The Nazis had no economic policies, so people voted for them randomly
questions.answer: The Nazis specifically promised strong leadership, jobs, and national revival, directly targeting the fears mass unemployment created
questions.why: It's not enough to say the Depression made Germans angry in general — the Nazis actively targeted unemployed and desperate voters with tailored promises of work and strength, which is why support specifically shifted to them rather than spreading evenly across parties.
